column3: “With” is added twice to join the verbless clauses.
“Was pregnant and crying out” puts the present tense in the past.
“Swept … from the sky, tossing them” renders “drags … of heaven and cast them”; “ready to” is added.
“Will rule” renders μέλλει ποιμαίνειν (“is about to shepherd”); “iron scepter” renders “rod of iron.”
“Where God had prepared a place for her” recasts “where she has there a place prepared by God.”
BSB follows the critical text with the singular “the dragon was not strong enough”; “for him and his angels” renders “for them.”
“Hurled down” renders ἐβλήθη; “the deceiver of” recasts “who deceives.”
“So as to shy away from death” renders “unto death.”
BSB follows the critical text with “woe to the earth and the sea”; the Textus Receptus has “woe to those who dwell on the earth and the sea.”
“From the presence of the serpent” is moved forward; “was nourished” renders the present “is nourished.”
“To overtake the woman and sweep her away in the torrent” recasts “after the woman … that he might cause her to be carried away by a flood.”
BSB follows the critical text with “Jesus” (the Textus Receptus has “Jesus Christ”). BSB includes here “And the dragon stood on the shore of the sea,” which the Greek counts as verse 18.
BSB has no text at this verse number; its content is in verse 17.
